in_text_mentions: No complications occurred, in particular no excessive bleeding, neither during the surgery nor in the week after. Mandibular sensitivity returned with the pass of the dental anesthesia. Seven days after surgery, the sutures were removed. Initial histologic examination revealed a dentigerous cyst (Figure 3). One year after surgery, a new panoramic radiograph was performed, revealing the complete healing of the site (Figure 2).

Bleeding is more likely to result from repetitive pressure or trauma on the overlying oral mucosa from the denture and is least likely to be from the cyst. The differential diagnosis considered a hemorrhagic eruptive cyst, but we considered this theory unlikely due to the age of the patient. The histological examination reported in Figure 3 confirmed the nature of the dentigerous cyst.

Revista cientifica odontologica (Universidad Cientifica del Sur) 2022. doi:10.21142/2523-2754-1002-2022-111. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Histopahological section.
in_text_mentions: The histopathological study showed a cystic tumor lined all around by a completely uniform non-keratinized stratified flat epithelium. Likewise, a basal membrane formed by some squamous cells that did not present any involvement was observed, and no evidence of granulosa cells was observed on the surface of the wall. Additionally, the contour of the cystic structure of the tumor was not altered, and there were some areas slightly formed by mature fibroblasts. Finally, the histopathological diagnosis was established as a dentigerous cyst (Figure 5).

panels.rationale: Single-panel pre-treatment orthopantomogram from a dentigerous cyst case report shows a unilocular radiolucency associated with the crown of an impacted lower right third molar, matching the target disease and supported by caption/in-text findings.

in_text_mentions: The orthopantomography revealed a unilocular cystic radiolucency that began at the resorbed root apex of the second molar, extended to the horizontally impacted third molar, and involved the right mandibular angle. The cyst was limited to the crown of the impacted third molar and extended down to the lower border of the mandible (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Single H&E histopathology panel from a confirmed dentigerous cyst case; caption and in-text histopathologic description support the diagnosis and specific findings.
panels.attribution_text: Batra et al. Management and Rehabilitation of Dentigerous Cyst With 10-Year Follow-Up: A Case Report.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.67867. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological examination of the cyst Magnification: 40x
in_text_mentions: Histopathological investigation revealed a cystic cavity lined by two- to three-layer thick epithelium with characteristics similar to reduced enamel epithelium. The epithelium connective tissue interface was flat. The underlying connective tissue capsule was fibrous with mild chronic inflammatory cells infiltrated. A few areas of extravasculated red blood cells (RBCs) were also appreciable along with peripheral areas exhibiting reactive bone formation. The histopathologic examination confirmed the diagnosis of a dentigerous cyst (Figure 3).

findings.evidence: well-defined unilocular radiolucency surrounding the crown of horizontally impacted 48

panels.rationale: CBCT of the mandible shows a well-defined unilocular radiolucency around the crown of horizontally impacted tooth 48, consistent with a classic dentigerous cyst. Caption and in-text support dentigerous cyst; annotations mark the inferior alveolar nerve canal.
panels.attribution_text: Varshney et al. Immunohistochemical Expression of Calretinin in Dentigerous Cyst Transforming Into Unicystic Ameloblastoma: A Case Report.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.68938. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: CBCT showing a well-defined unilocular radiolucency surrounding the crown of horizontally impacted 48 CBCT: Cone beam computed tomography
in_text_mentions: ding anterior-posteriorly from the cementoenamel junction (CEJ) of tooth 48 to the distal aspect of tooth 47 and superior-inferiorly from the crestal bone to approximately 8.8 mm from the inferior border of the mandible. Apically displaced right inferior alveolar nerve canal (IANC) was noted. Thinning/Discontinuity of both buccal and lingual cortical plate with respect to tooth 48 was seen. No signs of root resorption or fracture were noted with respect to tooth 47. Infra-erupted tooth 47 and approximation of right IANC with both mesial and distal roots of tooth 47 was also seen (Figures 2-3).

panels.rationale: Single-panel panoramic radiograph of a real patient with a case-report-confirmed dentigerous cyst: an impacted mandibular left first premolar is surrounded by a well-defined pericoronal radiolucency, matching the classic radiographic appearance of a dentigerous cyst (corticated radiolucency around the crown of an unerupted tooth). No demographic data or ethnicity stated in the caption or provided in-text mentions; radiograph shows no skin, so skin tone is null.

in_text_mentions: A panoramic radiograph revealed mandibular skeletal asymmetry between the right and left sides, together with mild alveolar bone crest resorption in the posterior regions of both arches. The mandibular left first premolar was impacted, positioned adjacent to the root of the mandibular left first primary molar, and surrounded by a well-defined pericoronal radiolucency (Fig. 2).

panels.rationale: Single orthopantomogram from a dentigerous cyst case report, showing the classic radiographic appearance of a well-defined radiolucent lesion surrounding the crown of an unerupted mandibular left second premolar. The article title and caption support dentigerous cyst attribution. No age, ethnicity, or skin tone information is provided in the caption or in-text mentions.
panels.attribution_text: Ghandour et al. Conservative Treatment of Dentigerous Cyst by Marsupialization in a Young Female Patient: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.. Case reports in dentistry 2018. doi:10.1155/2018/7621363. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Orthopantomogram (OPG) showing a radiolucent lesion at the mandibular left side (second premolar region).
in_text_mentions: clinical examination, the patient had all her permanent teeth and a retained mandibular left second primary molar. Radiographic records consisted of an orthopantomogram, a lateral cephalogram, a posteroanterior cephalogram, and a hand wrist radiograph. The orthopantomogram revealed a well-defined radiolucent lesion on the mandibular left side surrounding the unerupted mandibular left second premolar which appeared to be mesially tipped below the retained primary second molar. The root of the adjacent premolar was included in the lesion but did not reveal any root resorption (Figures 1 and 2).

panels.attribution_text: Barbeiro et al. Maxillary dentigerous cyst showing squamous odontogenic tumor-like proliferation: surgical approach and literature review.. Autopsy & case reports 2021. doi:10.4322/acr.2021.302. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Panoramic radiography showing a unilocular radiolucent lesion associated with tooth #18 displaced into the maxillary sinus.
in_text_mentions: A 42-year-old man was referred to our service with gingival bleeding at the level of the upper right second permanent molar. According to the patient, previous periodontal treatment was performed without any clinical improvement. Intraoral examination revealed an asymptomatic, slight expansion of the buccal cortical bone at the level of the molar region. Radiographic examination revealed a well-circumscribed ovoid radiolucency around the crown of tooth #18, which was displaced into the maxillary sinus (Figure 1).

panels.figure_caption: Axial view of CBCT revealed a well-defined solitary radiolucent lesion of approximately 16.5 × 20.7 × 14.2 mm (AP × SI × BL) with respect to the right posterior mandibular anterior ramus region, extending anteroposteriorly from CEJ of 48 to distal aspect of 47, and superoinferiorly from crestal bone to approximately 8.8 mm from inferior border of mandible. CBCT: Cone beam computed tomography; AP: Anteroposterior; SI: Superoinferior; BL: Buccolingual; CEJ: Cementoenamel junction
in_text_mentions: ding anterior-posteriorly from the cementoenamel junction (CEJ) of tooth 48 to the distal aspect of tooth 47 and superior-inferiorly from the crestal bone to approximately 8.8 mm from the inferior border of the mandible. Apically displaced right inferior alveolar nerve canal (IANC) was noted. Thinning/Discontinuity of both buccal and lingual cortical plate with respect to tooth 48 was seen. No signs of root resorption or fracture were noted with respect to tooth 47. Infra-erupted tooth 47 and approximation of right IANC with both mesial and distal roots of tooth 47 was also seen (Figures 2-3).

in_text_mentions: 5 cm, which was attached to the neck of the left mandibular second premolar and the apical view showed the apical displacement of the tooth bud (Figs 6A and B). panels.rationale: Single H&E histopathology panel of a human mandibular surgical specimen from a patient with an infected complex odontoma associated with a dentigerous cyst. The caption and in-text mentions describe the fibrous cyst wall lined focally by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which is the defining histologic feature of a dentigerous cyst; the odontomatous tissue and chronic osteitis are co-existing/complicating elements (recorded as proposed findings, as they are not in the allowed vocabulary). No skin, mucosa or clinical surface is shown, so skin tone and ethnicity are not assessable and no demographic data are given.
panels.attribution_text: Raâdani. Infected Complex Odontoma Associated With a Dentigerous Cyst Presenting as a Cutaneous Fistula in the Mandibular Angle: Surgical Management Using Piezoelectric Surgery. Case Reports in Dentistry 2026. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 7.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological examination of the mandibular specimen showing a complex odontoma associated with a dentigerous cyst and chronic osteitis (hematoxylin and eosin [H&E] staining, ×100 magnification). The upper portion shows a well‐demarcated nodule of acellular eosinophilic dental tissue consistent with odontomatous tissue. The middle portion shows the dense fibrous connective tissue forming the cyst wall. The lower portion demonstrates irregular necrotic bony trabeculae consistent with chronic osteitis.
in_text_mentions: a thick band of dense fibrous connective tissue forming the cyst wall. Focally, the inner surface of this fibrous wall was lined by a thin, nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium corresponding to the cystic lining. The lower portion showed marked pathological bone remodeling, with irregular and eroded necrotic bony trabeculae exhibiting empty osteocyte lacunae. The intertrabecular spaces were extensively occupied by a dense polymorphous inflammatory infiltrate and granulation tissue, characterized by numerous inflammatory cells, supporting the diagnosis of chronic osteitis. (Figure 7).

The in-text description explicitly lists dentigerous cyst first in the differential (with unicystic ameloblastoma and AOT) and the finding vocabulary matches the dentigerous cyst keys; because the radiograph cannot distinguish the associated AOT component, attribution is to the dentigerous cyst with moderate confidence.

findings.evidence: Buccal as well as lingual cortical perforation

panels.rationale: Single orthopantomogram from a dentigerous cyst case report showing a unilocular non-corticated radiolucency in the right posterior mandible extending to the mid-ramus, with in-text mention of root resorption of tooth 47 and buccal/lingual cortical perforation. The image is a real patient radiograph and supports dentigerous cyst attribution, though the non-corticated large appearance is a less common variant.

in_text_mentions: On radiological examination, orthopantomogram (OPG) revealed unilocular, non-corticated radiolucency on the right side extending from the tooth 47 region till the mid-ramus region. The internal structure was homogenously radiolucent. Buccal as well as lingual cortical perforation with root resorption of tooth with respect to tooth 47 was noted (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Single-panel panoramic radiograph of a real patient from a case report titled 'Mandibular Fracture Associated with a Dentigerous Cyst'. The in-text description specifies a well-defined mandibular radiolucency spanning the first premolar to second molar region with displacement of the lower left second premolar toward the inferior border and an associated pathological fracture, matching dentigerous cyst radiographic findings (well-corticated radiolucency, unerupted/displaced tooth crown, cortical expansion/bone destruction). No ethnicity or age stated in caption or text; skin tone not assessable on a radiograph. The 'L' laterality marker is an annotation.
panels.attribution_text: Kouhsoltani et al. Mandibular Fracture Associated with a Dentigerous Cyst: Report of a Case and Literature Review.. Journal of dental research, dental clinics, dental prospects 2015. doi:10.15171/joddd.2015.035. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: hically, a well-defined radiolucency was identified in the body of the mandible on the left side. The radiolucency extended from the first premolar region to the second molar area. It seemed to have destroyed bone almost from the edentulous alveolar crest to the inferior border of the mandible. A small ill-defined area was observed in the anterior border of the lesion. The lesion was associated with an obvious bony fracture in the inferior border of the mandible. The relatively large size of the lesion had pushed the lower left second premolar to the inferior border of the mandible (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: lined by a non-keratinized thin stratified epithelium (H&E 20x)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a real patient histology image showing the classic dentigerous cyst lining: a non-keratinized thin stratified squamous epithelium with a fibrous connective tissue wall. The article and in-text histopathological diagnosis identify dentigerous cyst. B: Panel B is a real patient histology image from the dentigerous cyst case showing basophilic ovoid calcifications in the connective wall and odontogenic epithelial cords. Calcifications are a less common variant feature of this dentigerous cyst. C: Panel C is a real patient histology image from the dentigerous cyst case showing ovoid calcifications with peripheral eosinophilic areas and irregular disposition. These calcifications represent the variant dentigerous cyst with capsular/intracystic calcifications described in the article.
panels.attribution_text: Borrás-Ferreres et al. Dentigerous cyst with parietal and intracystic calcifications: A case report and literature review.. Journal of clinical and experimental dentistry 2018. doi:10.4317/jced.54505. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: A) Cystic lesion with a fibrous connective wall without signs of inflammation and lined by a non-keratinized thin stratified epithelium (H&E 20x). B) Basophilic ovoid calcifications present at the connective wall and odontogenic epithelial cords (H&E 20x). C) Ovoid calcifications and peripheral eosinophilic areas with irregular disposition (H&E 40x).
in_text_mentions: Microscopically, a cystic wall constituted by fibrous connective tissue was observed. Interestingly, some basophilic globular calcified ovoid deposits were seen into its thickness. Furthermore, some of these had a greater size and presented a cemento-osseous structure with apposition lines and included cells. Some capsular deposits showed a non-keratinized stratified thin epithelial lining, focally detached (Fig. 2). The histopathological diagnosis was dentigerous cyst with capsular calcifications.

in_text_mentions: A 38‐year‐old male presented to a private oral and maxillofacial radiology center for a routine panoramic radiograph. The imaging revealed a large radiolucent lesion in the right maxilla, leading to referral to a maxillofacial surgeon for further evaluation (Figure 1). The patient's medical history was unremarkable, with no history of systemic disease, trauma, or previous maxillofacial surgery. He reported no known allergies and was not taking any medications. Regarding habits, the patient denied smoking, alcohol consumption, or parafunctional habits such as bruxism.

panels.rationale: Single-panel H&E photomicrograph (HES, ×20) from a dentigerous cyst case report; the caption describes a non-keratinizing epithelial lining without rete pegs and a fibrous wall with rare inflammatory cells, and the in-text mentions state that histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of a dentigerous cyst. The image is a real patient tissue section showing the characteristic thin non-keratinized squamous epithelial lining of a dentigerous cyst, supporting the squamous epithelial lining finding; the sparse inflammatory infiltrate is insufficient to tag chronic inflammation of the cyst wall.

in_text_mentions: daily for 10 days). After nine months, a considerable decrease of the lesion was observed on panoramic radiography (not shown). Excision of the cystic lesion, as well as extraction of the impacted mandibular right second molar, was then performed. Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of a dentigerous cyst (Figure 4). One year later, a new panoramic radiography was carried out showing a complete mandible bone healing (Figure 5). The mandibular right third molar was only removed after its migration to the retromolar region in order to cause the least surgical trauma (Figure 5).

in_text_mentions: aphy was performed to evaluate the impacted third molars. The imaging showed a horizontally impacted mandibular right third molar (48) and a mesioangularly impacted mandibular left third molar (38). A well-defined ovoid hypodense lesion was noted surrounding the crown of tooth 48, suggestive of a cystic lesion. The lesion measured approximately 13.8 × 15.4 × 9.7 mm and extended to the distal root of tooth 47, with associated bone loss. The mesial aspect of the crown of 48 was in close contact with the distal surface of 47. No root resorption or caries was observed in relation to 47 (Figure 1).

in_text_mentions: m as well as columnar cells in the periphery and cuboidal cells in the basal region. The capsule consisted of dense conjunctive tissue and exhibited multiple cordon-nest-like structures typical of odontogenic epithelium. In some areas, there was a tissue with myxoid appearance and in others it was possible to identify inflammatory infiltrate which was predominantly lymphoplasmocitary, ranging from discrete to moderate. A: Axial CBCT of the mandible showing a unilocular corticated radiolucency involving the crowns of developing teeth and displacing adjacent structures, consistent with dentigerous cyst. Revista cientifica odontologica (Universidad Cientifica del Sur) 2022. doi:10.21142/2523-2754-1002-2022-111. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.

in_text_mentions: he germ of tooth 36, being unilocular and surrounded by a hyperdense line, with involvement of the germ of tooth 37, scalloping the adjacent dental structures and generating displacement of tooth 75 (Figure 2). Additionally, displacement and erosion of the vestibular bone table with thinning of the lingual bone table was observed, establishing a presumptive radiographic diagnosis of cystic lesion to rule out dentigerous cyst versus infected mandibular buccal cyst. In addition, the presence of a hypodense lesion with similar imaging characteristics was visualized in the contra lateral quadrant.

in_text_mentions: homogenous and radiolucent with no obvious internal calcifications or septae. There was expansion and attenuation of the cortical bone on both the buccal and lingual surfaces, with intermittent breach of the lingual cortex and buccal cortex in the third molar region. There was inferior displacement of the right inferior alveolar canal with thinning and possibly partial effacement of the superior cortex and resultant scalloping of the mandibular inferior cortex was also seen. The lesion had caused apical root resorption of the right second molar as noted in the panoramic radiograph (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: H&E section of a human dentigerous cyst showing cystic lumen, epithelial lining and fibrous capsule; caption and in-text explicitly confirm the diagnosis of DC. b: H&E section showing inflamed dentigerous cyst wall with arcading epithelial hyperplasia, explicitly attributed to the DC in the in-text description. c: H&E section of thin non-keratinized epithelial lining resembling reduced enamel epithelium, which the in-text states confirmed the diagnosis of dentigerous cyst.
panels.attribution_text: Shaji et al. Successful Preservation of a Developing Unerupted Tooth Associated With Dentigerous Cyst in a Child: A Case Report.. Case reports in dentistry 2025. doi:10.1155/crid/6972721. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological findings of the lesion: (a) cystic lumen showing lumen, epithelial lining, and connective tissue capsule; (b) hyperplasia as interconnecting epithelial strands with connective tissue stroma entrapped within giving an arcading pattern; and (c) thin epithelium resembling reduced enamel epithelium.
in_text_mentions: lumen, epithelial lining, and connective tissue capsule. The epithelial lining was composed of nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium and shows hyperplasia as interconnecting epithelial strands with connective tissue stroma entrapped within giving an arcading pattern. The connective tissue showed a dense infiltrate of chronic inflammatory cells, predominantly lymphocytes. At areas where the inflammatory infiltrate was minimal, the epithelium was thin, composed of two to four layers of flattened cells resembling reduced enamel epithelium, which confirmed the diagnosis of a DC (Figure 4).

Unresorbed roots of the previously endodontically treated deciduous second molars were in direct contact with the cystic cavity, including a second premolar's crown protruding into the cavity. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Low-power H&E of a dentigerous cyst showing a cystic lumen lined by hyperplastic non-keratinized squamous epithelium with chronic inflammatory cells in the fibrous capsule, matching the caption and in-text diagnostic confirmation. b: Higher-magnification H&E showing the cystic cavity lined by hyperplastic non-keratinized epithelium with adjacent chronic inflammatory infiltrate and fibrous connective tissue, characteristic of dentigerous cyst. c: High-power H&E of the fibrous cystic capsule densely infiltrated by chronic inflammatory cells, a histologic feature of the dentigerous cyst wall described in the caption and text.

panels.figure_caption: Microscopic findings of the sample Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E). (a) Low-powered magnification (10×). (b) Cystic cavity lined by hyperplastic non-keratinized epithelium. (c) Chronic inflammatory cells in fibrous connective tissue of the cystic capsule.
in_text_mentions: Microscopic analysis of the sample material confirmed the diagnosis of a dentigerous cyst. It was also noted that the fibrous cystic wall contained an infiltrate with a large number of chronic inflammatory cells. in_text_mentions: ced on the right side of the face extending from the body of the mandible to almost the ramus with limited mouth opening. Palpation revealed a nontender, nonpulsatile, bony hard swelling with no local rise in temperature (Figure 1a). The overlying skin appeared normal. On intraoral examination, a firm, nontender swelling was noted in the right buccal vestibule extending till the retromolar pad causing vestibular obliteration. The overlying mucosa was intact, with no signs of ulceration or discharge. Grossly decayed lower right deciduous second molar was noted. No vitality test was carried out.
The orthopantomogram (OPG) revealed a unilocular, radiolucent lesion with a well-defined radiopaque border associated with unerupted mandibular right second premolar (Figure 1b).

in_text_mentions: uamous epithelium with focal areas of rete ridges proliferating into the connective tissue stroma. Scattered mucous cells were also seen in the epithelial lining. The underlying connective tissue revealed loosely arranged collagen fibers in a myxoid stroma, diffuse chronic inflammatory cell infiltrate areas of extravasated RBCs, odontogenic cell rests, and cholesterol clefts. Based on the histopathological correlation, a diagnosis of an infected/inflamed dentigerous cyst was given (Figure 1D and Figure 2). The patient's immediate and one-year follow-ups revealed no recurrence (Figures 1E, 1F).

findings.label: Well-corticated radiolucency around crown
findings.evidence: Radiographically, the lesion appeared as a well‐circumscribed, corticated, unilocular radiolucency

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial CBCT reconstruction from a case of a large dentigerous cyst associated with an impacted supernumerary tooth; shows a well-corticated unilocular radiolucency enclosing the unerupted tooth crown in the right maxilla, matching the captioned radiographic description. B: Coronal CBCT view of the same dentigerous cyst, showing the corticated radiolucency and the impacted supernumerary tooth contained within it. C: Sagittal CBCT view demonstrating the outline and vertical extent of the corticated cystic lesion containing the supernumerary tooth. D: Three-dimensional CBCT reconstruction of the same patient's maxilla showing the extent of the dentigerous cyst and the impacted supernumerary tooth; a real patient CT-derived image.
panels.attribution_text: Bashiri and Mohebiniya. Surgical Management of a Large Dentigerous Cyst Associated With an Impacted Supernumerary Tooth: A Rare Case Report.. Clinical case reports 2026. doi:10.1002/ccr3.73015. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Axial (A), coronal (B), sagittal (C), and three‐dimensional (D) views clearly demonstrate the lesion's outline and extent, as well as the impacted supernumerary tooth.
in_text_mentions: ation prompted the surgeon to request a cone‐beam computed tomography (CBCT) scan for detailed assessment. CBCT analysis demonstrated a large, localized, unilateral lesion within the right maxillary bone (Figure 2). Multiplanar reconstructions—including axial, sagittal, coronal, and 3D views—showed that the lesion extended from the periapical region of the left central incisor to that of the right first molar, and vertically from the alveolar crest to the superior two‐thirds of the right maxillary sinus. The lesion measured 28 mm vertically, 21 mm buccopalatally, and 33.5 mm anteroposteriorly.

Comprehensive CBCT analysis revealed the presence of two supernumerary teeth (mesiodentes). The first was located at the midline and showed no pathological association. The second was displaced laterally and was entirely encompassed within the lesion, suggesting its direct involvement in cystic development. Radiographically, the lesion appeared as a well‐circumscribed, corticated, unilocular radiolucency completely enclosing the supernumerary tooth (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Single H&E photomicrograph of a real patient's jaw cyst specimen showing a non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelial lining over a fibrous connective tissue wall, a finding explicitly listed in the dentigerous cyst vocabulary and captioned here. The article concerns a glandular odontogenic cyst mimicking a dentigerous cyst, so the disease attribution carries some uncertainty and confidence is moderate; no other disease is named in the caption for this panel.

panels.figure_caption: Photomicrograph showing non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelial lining of variable thickness with an underlying fibrous connective tissue capsule (H&E stain, 100x).
in_text_mentions: The epithelial lining was non-keratinised stratified squamous. It exhibited variable thickness (Figure 7), ranging from flattened to cuboidal cells, with focal areas showing epithelial plaque-like thickenings. Numerous intraepithelial microcystic spaces were evident (Figure 8). The superficial layer demonstrated eosinophilic cuboidal cells with characteristic hobnail morphology. These cells showed apocrine snouting. Occasional ciliated cells were also observed. Additionally, scattered clear cells were present (Figures 9-11).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Coronal CT of a real patient showing a radiolucent lesion in the right maxillary sinus containing the crown of an impacted right maxillary third molar, the provisional diagnosis being dentigerous cyst. Confidence is limited because the article ultimately reports the lesion as a follicular odontogenic keratocyst mimicking a dentigerous cyst, so the true histologic nature is not a dentigerous cyst; age group taken from the patient data burned into the CT image (22F), not from the caption text. b: Axial CT of the same patient showing the radiolucent lesion of the right maxillary sinus enclosing the impacted right maxillary third molar crown, provisionally diagnosed as a dentigerous cyst. Same caveat as panel a: the final diagnosis in the report is a follicular odontogenic keratocyst mimicking a dentigerous cyst, so disease attribution rests on the provisional clinical-radiographic diagnosis and the article's dentigerous-cyst focus.

panels.rationale: Single panoramic radiograph from a case report titled 'Unusual Imaging Features of Dentigerous Cyst.' The caption and in-text describe a well-defined multiloculated radiolucent lesion involving an impacted mandibular right second molar, supporting dentigerous cyst with atypical multilocular imaging.

in_text_mentions: linical diagnosis of ameloblastoma having hemi-mandibulectomy as the suggested therapy. At admission, no relevant aspects within his medical history were observed. He brought a panoramic radiography (Figure 1) which revealed the presence of a multilocular lesion involving the impacted mandibular right second molar suggesting mainly an ameloblastoma or an OKC. It extended from the right mandibular notch to the lower right first premolar. A displacement of the mandibular canal and the lower right third molar towards the mandibular notch was also observed.
